svg.title: The Two-Contract Double Close Sequence
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-01-double-close-sequence; chapter number: 1; chart type: process_flow; title: The Two-Contract Double Close Sequence; subtitle: Two contracts, two independent closings, the end buyer's cash in escrow first; caption: Wholesalers, title operators and transactional lenders run the same five moves so the seller never sees the resale price and the end buyer never sees the buy price.; assumptions note: Fees shown are the quoted rates of Flip Lab Capital (1% to 3% of purchase) and Bright Closings (1% plus $100 above $75,000, flat $850 below). Practitioners split on whether leg one must close with outside cash or with the end buyer's wire.; note: Attributed to Jerry Norton (Flipping Mastery TV), Ricky (Flip Lab), Jasper Cool, Ryan Schrope and Game Changer Real Estate Insights.; stages: step: 01; label: Lock the cash buyer deposit; value: Step 1; detail: Jerry Norton requires a $2,500 minimum non-refundable deposit, $5,000 to $10,000 preferred, backed by a release clause needing no further escrow instruction.; step: 02; label: Write the closer into both contracts; value: Step 2; detail: Insert 'seller or buyer agrees to use the closing services of' plus an investor-friendly title company, because the wrong title company will kill the deal.; step: 03; label: Screen REO and short sale deed limits; value: Step 3; detail: Game Changer Real Estate Insights checks bank-owned and short sale deeds for resale bans of 30, 60 or 90 days before promising a double close.; step: 04; label: Confirm end buyer cash in escrow; value: Step 4; detail: Flip Lab funds only after title confirms the end buyer's funds are there; Ryan Schrope moves no money on the A leg until B-to-C funds land.; step: 05; label: Fund leg A and repay from leg B-to-C; value: Step 5; detail: Funder wires the A-to-B purchase and is repaid on the B-to-C leg, often within an hour; a $100,000 purchase at Bright Closings costs $1,100 out of the second closing.
